object_description: freestanding circular collection building paired with an orthogonal covered work-yard structure
design_condition: The two buildings are separated across the perimeter, leaving flowing landscape space open while placing the work yard near the existing yard and linking the ensemble through future open-air-museum development.

positive.statement: The setting leaves a great deal of flowing landscape space open and maintains a relaxed relationship to the surroundings.
The protective circle is architecturally and structurally clearly articulated.
The calm, reserved building avoids monumentality despite its circular shape.
The geometrical relationship between periphery and content leads to good operational processes.
The central depot enables the shortest possible routes to the excavated objects.
The canopy creates a transition between inside and outside and an adaptable work zone.
The circular form creates a relaxed yet attractive spatial experience.
The project’s architectural, functional, and economic approach is convincing.
The unexpected interplay of classic typologies and construction methods creates an ensemble with independent identity.

negative.statement: Separating the depot creates distances and traffic routes that have to be bridged.
The need to import the earth somewhat diminishes the coherence of the concept.
The proposed horizontal bracing in the rammed-earth wall is problematic because of differing creep behavior.
